statements.quote: Both the independent-samples t tests (Table 2; p values ranging from .010 to <.001) and the multilevel analyses without control variables (Supplemental Materials S4; p values ranging from .006 to <.001) find a consistent treatment effect across all three creativity measures (i.e., supervisor-rated creativity, external-rater-rated novelty, and external-rater-rated usefulness). In the main text, we include models with control variables and additional mediators, which lead to attenuated direct effects of LLM assistance on creativity outcomes.

notes: Read all 536 lines of the supplied markdown (the complete 14-page Online First PDF, including references; no appendix is embedded) and checked the relevant original PDF pages. Also retrieved and read all 10 pages of the separately linked publisher supplement in memory. The source-of-record availability statement explicitly says the firm confidentiality agreement prevents public data sharing and that data and materials are available upon request; it also says the study was not preregistered. The form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are empty. No study repository or code URL is named in the article or supplement. The only public deposit found is the aggregate supplemental PDF; on_request describes access to the participant-level study data, not access to that PDF. No public participant-level or participant-linked output data were found in the repository API searches. Initial Zenodo searches returned HTTP 400 because size=100 exceeds the anonymous limit; using the permitted size=25 returned HTTP 200. Successful queries and broad-query result counts are recorded above; the 143 DataCite broad-name hits were inspected across two pages. OSF queries used the requested public node title filter, including for the author's name, and are not exhaustive searches of all project contributors. The main publisher landing-page request, https://doi.org/10.1037/apl0001296, redirected to https://doi.apa.org/doi/10.1037/apl0001296 and returned HTTP 403 with an Incapsula bot-check page; inspection stopped there. The separately cited supplement loaded without credentials. No login, access request, CAPTCHA solving, or bot-check bypass was attempted. Relative to final.open_items, the missing supplement is now available: Table S5 on supplement p. 6 is explicitly the no-controls table, including Model 4 for usefulness; Table S4 on p. 5 concerns item-level usefulness models. This resolves the conflicting S5-versus-S4 locator by inspection, but is not a computation from raw data. No additional participant-level statistics can be computed from the public files: arm-specific randomized/analyzed counts and numeric arm-mean SEs remain unavailable, and diversity cannot be calculated without the participants' texts. Table 2 of the main article already prints arm means and SDs. AI availability during the response task and external-rater qualifications remain unconfirmed. Quotes preserve the source wording with line wrapping and PDF ligatures normalized; routine descriptions of data collection and cited third-party literature are not treated as data-availability links.
